With any `nano-banana` model the image is always `3:4`, whatever `aspect_ratio` says; the GPT Image models keep your `aspect_ratio`. `nano-banana` then runs on `nano-banana-pro`, so a pose with `nano-banana` or `nano-banana-pro` needs a Pro plan or higher (`402` otherwise).

prompt.description: A description of the image to generate. A prompt of only whitespace returns `400`.

output.description: The results, or `null` until the task succeeds.

TextToImageTask.description: A Text to Image task (`type` is `text-to-image`), single image or multi-view.

TextToMotionOutput.description: The `output` of a Text to Motion task.

mode.description: The mode the clip was made with.

motion_url.description: The motion clip, as an FBX file for `prime` or a BVH file for `swift`.

duration.description: The clip length in seconds, from 2 to 10 in steps of 0.5, such as `3` or `4.5`. Other values return 400 `duration must be between 2 and 10 seconds in 0.5 second steps`.

mode.description: The motion model: `prime` returns an FBX clip, and `swift` returns a BVH clip. The two modes cost different amounts.

prompt.description: The motion to generate, up to 400 characters, such as `A person waves with the right hand, then takes a bow`. A prompt of only spaces returns 400 `prompt must not be empty`. Prompts in other languages are translated to English.

output.description: The results, or `null` until the task succeeds.

TextToMotionTask.description: A Text to Motion task (`type` is `text-to-motion`).

TextureURLs.description: One item per texture set. Never `null` once the task has succeeded; empty for an untextured result. Each item has all six maps, and a map the task didn't produce is `null`.

ThumbnailURLs.description: Previews of the model from four sides. A view that failed to render is left out.

input_task_id.description: A `SUCCEEDED` task of yours, created with the API, that produced a 3D model, such as Text to 3D, Image to 3D or Remesh. UV Unwrap reads the task's GLB. Required unless `model_url` is sent.

model_url.description: The model to unwrap, as a public http(s) URL whose path ends in `.glb`, or a data URI (`data:model/gltf-binary;base64,...`), up to 400 MB from a URL or 100 MB as a `data:` URI. A GLB over 100 MB must not use Draco compression. Only GLB files are supported; to unwrap another format, run Convert to GLB first and pass that task's `id` as `input_task_id`. Required unless `input_task_id` is sent.

output.description: The results, or `null` until the task succeeds.

data.description: The usage records on this page. Empty, never `null`, when there are none.

has_more.description: `true` when there's another page. There's no total count.

UsageRecord.description: One finished API task and the credits it used. Metadata only, with no file links.

api_key_name.description: The name of the API key that ran the task, or `Meshy CLI` for a task run with a Meshy CLI login. An empty string when the task was never charged, when the key has been deleted, or when the task ran through another app's login.

api_key_suffix.description: The last four characters of that API key, to tell keys with the same name apart. An empty string whenever `api_key_name` is empty, and for Meshy CLI logins.

consumed_credits.description: Credits the task used, after refunds. `0` for a failed task and for free tasks such as Analyze Printability.

created_at.description: When the task was created, in Unix milliseconds.

endpoint.description: The task's type, such as `image-to-3d`, `rig` or `print-repair` (see `TaskType`). Text to 3D tasks show `text-to-3d-preview`, `text-to-3d-refine` or `text-to-3d`. Older records can carry names of retired endpoints, which the `endpoints` filter doesn't accept.

finished_at.description: When the task finished, in Unix milliseconds. `null` if the task has no finish time.

metadata.description: The tags sent in the `X-Meshy-Metadata` header when the task was created. `{}` if none.

task_id.description: The task's ID. A task you created can be read with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}` until it's deleted or expires; a teammate's task returns `404` there.

info.description:
Meshy API v2 gives every task one response shape (the task object), one set of task
routes (`/v2/tasks`), and one error format.

**Preview.** This specification is a preview. It isn't listed on the public site yet.

**Authentication.** Send your API key as a Bearer token:
`Authorization: Bearer msy_YOUR_API_KEY`. Create keys at
https://www.meshy.ai/developers/keys.

**Asynchronous model.** A create (`POST /v2/<endpoint>`) returns `202 Accepted` with the
task object (`status: PENDING`, your request in `input`, `output: null`), a `Location`
header (`/openapi/v2/tasks/{id}`) and a `Retry-After` header. Read the task with
`GET /v2/tasks/{id}` until `status` is `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED` or `CANCELED`, waiting
`Retry-After` seconds between reads, or stream it with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}/stream`.
On `SUCCEEDED`, the results are in `output`, whose fields depend on the task `type`.
Text to 3D is the one exception: its create response also keeps `result` (the task ID),
and its `Location` is `/openapi/v2/text-to-3d/{id}`. Read that task on `/v2/tasks` like
any other.

**Errors.** A request that fails returns an HTTP error with
`{"type": "...", "code": "...", "message": "...", "doc_url": ...}`, where `doc_url` is a
link or `null` (see `Error`). Branch on `code` or `type`, not on `message`: `400` bad
input, `401` missing or bad API key, `402` not enough credits, a credit limit, or a plan
that doesn't allow the request, `403` not allowed (an IP allowlist or content
moderation), `404` unknown task or route, `429` too many requests (wait `Retry-After`
seconds when the header is sent). The one exception is Text to 3D: a request it rejects
before reading the API key returns only `{"message": "..."}`. A task that fails later
has `status: FAILED` and a `task_error` object.

**Unknown parameters.** A create request with a top-level parameter the endpoint doesn't
define, such as a misspelled name or a removed v1 parameter, returns `400` with code
`parameter_unknown`. `message` names the parameter and what to send instead. Text to 3D
requests with `mode` ignore such a parameter.

**Choosing models.** Before the first create request, find out what the user is making,
for example a game character, a product render, or a 3D print. If they haven't said, ask.
Then pick the models from the "Choose by project" table at https://docs.meshy.ai/api/v2/models.md. Leaving `ai_model`
out gives Meshy 7.1, a dense, detailed mesh that doesn't suit a low-poly game asset.
`texture_model` has no default: every request for a textured model names one.

**Scope.** Every v2 create, the `/v2/tasks` routes, `/v2/balance`, `/v2/usage/tasks`
and `/v2/animations/library`. Not included: Creative Lab (v1 only) and the legacy
Text to 3D read routes under `/v2/text-to-3d/{id}` (read every task on `/v2/tasks`).

post.description: Makes a rigged character move: applies one animation from the library (`action_id`), several of them joined into one file (`action_ids`), or a clip from Text to Motion (`motion_task_id`). Find library IDs with `GET /v2/animations/library`. Each animation in a task is charged, so a task with `action_ids` costs more than one with `action_id` or `motion_task_id`. Returns the task object (`type: animate`) with 202; read the result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with `status` PENDING, your request in `input` and `output` null.

get.description: Returns the animations in the library, with the `action_id` to send when you create an Animation task. The filters combine; without any, you get the whole library. The response is a bare array ordered by `action_id`, not a page: there is no `data` wrapper and no pagination. Calling it is free.

post.description: Converts a 3D model to other file formats, from a Meshy task (`input_task_id`) or your own model file (`model_url`). On v2, a `model_url` upload keeps its size, and STL and 3MF files are scaled down to at most 150 mm on the longest side for a model Meshy generated (see `target_formats`). Returns the task object (`type: convert`) with 202; read the result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with `status` PENDING, your request in `input` and `output` null.

post.description: Turns one image into a 3D model, textured or untextured, in the formats you choose. Returns the task object with `202 Accepted`; its `type` is `image-to-3d`. The task runs in the background: read its result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`, stream it with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}/stream`, or get it by webhook.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with `status` PENDING, your request in `input` and `output` null.

post.description: Checks whether a 3D model is ready to print: holes, non-manifold edges, degenerate faces, and walls too thin for your printer. Wall thickness is always checked, by default for an FDM print 150 mm tall (see `PrintAnalyzeRequest`). It never changes the model. The endpoint is free (`consumed_credits` is 0) and works on every plan, including the free plan, so it never returns `402`. Returns `202` with the task object (`type` `print-analyze`). If `input_task_id` names a task Meshy has already analyzed at the same printer type and print size, the task is created already SUCCEEDED, the `202` body has the result in `output` and there is no `Retry-After` header; a webhook is still sent. Check `status` before you poll `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with your request in `input` and `consumed_credits` 0. Usually `status` is PENDING, `output` is null and `Retry-After` says when to read the task first. On a cached result (an `input_task_id` Meshy has already analyzed at the same printer type and print size), `status` is SUCCEEDED, `progress` is 100, `output.printability` holds the result and there is no `Retry-After` header. `Location` is always set.

403.description: Forbidden. The request came from an address outside the API key's IP allowlist, or `input_task_id` is a bas-relief task (`This model type does not support this operation`).

post.description: Turns a textured 3D model into a multi-color 3MF file, with the model's colors reduced to a filament palette and a slicer preset for your printer brand. The model must have color: a base color texture, or vertex colors for the `cartoon` style. Most inputs are checked when you create the task and return `400` if they lack the color that `style` needs; some, such as an `.fbx` upload, are only checked once the task runs, and the task then fails with `model_missing_texture`. The 3MF file has its origin at the bottom. For a model Meshy generated, it's scaled down to at most 150 mm on the longest side; uploaded and resized models keep their own size. Returns `202` with the task object (`type` `print-multi-color`). Read the result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with `status` PENDING, your request in `input` and `output` null.

post.description: Repairs a 3D model for printing: closes holes, fixes broken geometry, and thickens walls too thin for your printer. Wall thickness is always checked, by default for an FDM print 150 mm tall (see `PrintRepairRequest`). The model is never scaled. A repair takes about 20 seconds, or about 100 seconds when walls are thickened. Returns `202` with the task object (`type` `print-repair`); the top-level `intended_print` is already in that response. Read the result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with `status` PENDING, your request in `input` and `output` null.

post.description: Cuts a generated model into parts you can print separately, either where Meshy chooses or along the parts or colors you name, with optional connectors so the pieces fit back together. By default the parts come back as flat-colored geometry, without the input's texture; `keep_texture: true` keeps a textured input's texture on every part. With `mode` `by_parts` or `by_color`, Meshy reads your prompt before it answers, so the create request can take up to about a minute. Returns `202` with the task object (`type` `print-split`), plus top-level `prompt_ignored: true` when Meshy used the parts it identified instead of your prompt. Read the result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with `status` PENDING, your request in `input` and `output` null.

503.description: `Prompt parsing is busy right now; retry shortly`. Only for `mode` `by_parts` or `by_color`, when reading the prompt timed out. Nothing is charged. Retry later, or use `mode` `auto`.

post.description: Turns one photo into a bas-relief model (by default a GLB in meters; `target_formats` picks the formats, and `color_mapping` colors the GLB, OBJ, FBX, and USDZ with the photo) and a 16-bit grayscale depth map (PNG), for 3D printing, laser engraving and CNC carving. With `should_generate_model` `false`, the task makes the depth map only. Returns `202` with the task object (`type` `relief`). A Relief task can't be canceled, and endpoints that take a model as input (Remesh, Convert, Auto Split and others) refuse its ID with `403`. Read the result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with `status` PENDING, your request in `input` and `output` null.

post.description: Rebuilds a model's mesh with a new topology and face count, from a Meshy task (`input_task_id`) or your own model file (`model_url`), and returns it in the formats listed in `target_formats` (GLB by default). A `quad` mesh keeps its quads in OBJ and FBX files. For a real-world size, run Resize on the result. The v1 keys `resize_height`, `resize_longest_side`, `origin_at`, `auto_size` and `convert_format_only` were removed: a body that contains any of them returns 400, even when the value is `null` or `false`. Returns the task object (`type: remesh`) with 202; read the result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with `status` PENDING, your request in `input` and `output` null.

post.description: Scales a 3D model to a real-world size, in meters, and sets where its origin goes, from a Meshy task (`input_task_id`) or your own model file (`model_url`). Returns the task object (`type: resize`) with 202; read the result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with `status` PENDING, your request in `input` and `output` null.

post.description: Generates new textures for an existing 3D model from a text prompt, a reference image, or up to four views of the object. Returns the task object with `202 Accepted`; its `type` is `retexture`. The task runs in the background: read its result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`, stream it with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}/stream`, or get it by webhook.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with `status` PENDING, your request in `input` and `output` null.

post.description: Adds a skeleton to a character model so it can be animated. Every rigged character also comes with a walking and a running animation. To animate the rig, pass the task's `id` to `POST /v2/animations`. Returns 422 when the model can't be rigged, for example when no character is found in it. Returns the task object (`type: rig`) with 202; read the result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with `status` PENDING, your request in `input` and `output` null.

post.description: Creates a task that checks whether Meshy can rig and animate the model of one of your tasks, and which `animation_type` it fits, from the task's preview image. Returns `202` with the task object (`type` `rig-check`); read the answer in `output` with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}` when the task is SUCCEEDED. The check is optional: a Rigging task doesn't read it.

202.description: Task created. The body is the task object with your request in `input`. `Location` is always set, and `Retry-After` says when to read the task first while it hasn't finished.

get.description: Returns one page of your API tasks of every type, newest first by default, as `{"data": [...], "has_more": ...}`. Each item is a full task object, the same one `GET /v2/tasks/{id}` returns, except that `preceding_tasks` is always `0`. Tasks created on v1 are included. Creative Lab tasks are not, and neither are tasks whose files a team content check already withheld. There is no total count: request the next page while `has_more` is `true`.

delete.description: Deletes a task. This can't be undone, and the task then returns `404` on every route. Deleting a `PENDING` task refunds its credits. An `IN_PROGRESS` task can't be deleted (`409`): wait for a final status, then delete it. Creative Lab tasks can't be deleted here and return `404`. Returns `200` with an empty body.

404.description: No task with this ID belongs to your account, it is already deleted, or it is a Creative Lab task (`task_not_found`). `message` is `Task "<id>" not found`, with the ID in quotes.

get.description: Returns one task of any type, including tasks created on v1. Read every v2 task here: there are no per-endpoint read routes on v2. While the task is `PENDING` or `IN_PROGRESS`, the `Retry-After` header says how many seconds to wait before you get it again. Creative Lab tasks, and tasks that were not created through the API, return `404`.

200.description: The task object. `output` is shaped by `type`.

get.description: Streams a task's updates as Server-Sent Events until it reaches a final status. Each `message` event carries the full task object, the same JSON `GET /v2/tasks/{id}` returns. Once the stream is open the HTTP status stays `200`, and a problem with the task (such as an unknown ID) arrives as an `error` event, not as an HTTP error. Errors before the stream opens, such as a missing API key, are ordinary HTTP errors.

post.description:
Creates a Text to 3D task and returns the task object with `202`. The task runs in the
background: read its result with `GET /v2/tasks/{id}`, stream it, or get it by webhook.

One route makes three kinds of task, picked by `mode` and `should_texture`:

- Omit `mode` for a one-call task, `type` `text-to-3d`. `should_texture` (default `true`)
  picks a textured model, which needs `texture_model`, or the mesh only (`false`).
- `mode: preview` makes an untextured mesh, `type` `text-to-3d-preview`.
- `mode: refine` with `preview_task_id` textures a preview's mesh, `type` `text-to-3d-refine`.

The `type` filter `text-to-3d` on `GET /v2/tasks` lists all three kinds; `text-to-3d-preview`
and `text-to-3d-refine` list one kind each.

get.description:
Returns one page of your team's finished API tasks and the credits each one used, newest first by default, for billing exports and cost reports. Calling it is free. The API key must belong to an active member of a Studio or Enterprise team (any member, not only owners and admins); other keys get `403`.
Listed: tasks that finished as `SUCCEEDED` or `FAILED` and were created inside the window, by everyone who is a member of the team now, from any of their API keys, including deleted and expired tasks. Not listed: `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS` and `CANCELED` tasks, Creative Lab tasks, tasks run by Meshy's AI agents, and work done in the Meshy web app. If the team has a data retention period, the window starts no earlier than that period allows.

parameters.description: The start of the window, as an RFC 3339 timestamp such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`. Tasks created at or after this time are included. Defaults to 30 days before `end_time`. The window can span at most 366 days. In a URL, encode the `+` of an offset such as `+08:00` as `%2B`, or use `Z`.
parameters.name: start_time

parameters.description: The end of the window, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Tasks created before this time are included. Defaults to now. Must be after `start_time`.
parameters.name: end_time

parameters.description: A comma-separated list of the endpoints to include, by the same names as the `type` values (see `TaskType`), for example `text-to-3d,image-to-3d`. `text-to-3d` covers preview, refine and one-call Text to 3D tasks. Leave it out to include every endpoint. An unknown name returns `400`.
parameters.name: endpoints

parameters.description: Only tasks that finished with this status. Leave it out to include both.
